birds and vegetation of shade coffee plantations in chikmagalur, central western ghats, india

overview: this dataset contains bird community and vegetation data collected from 12 shade coffee plantation estates and two sites within bhadra tiger reserve in the chikmagalur district of karnataka, india, between december 2005 and may 2006. the data were collected as part of an msc thesis at the national centre for biological sciences and the centre for wildlife studies. the study examines how local-scale habitat properties and landscape-scale factors (viz. distance to contiguous forests) influence bird species richness and abundance in shade coffee plantations of the western ghats biodiversity hotspot.

associated publication: anand, m. o., krishnaswamy, j., and das, a. (2008). proximity to forests drives bird conservation value of coffee plantations: implications for certification. ecological applications, 18(7), 1754–1763. https://doi.org/10.1890/07-1839.1

study site: the fieldwork was conducted in the foothills of the bababudan hills, chikmagalur district, karnataka, india. coffee (arabica and robusta varieties) plantations in the district cover over 870 km² and contribute close to 25% of all coffee produced from the western ghats. plantations are almost entirely grown under a shade layer, which ranges from native shade trees to monocultures of the introduced species, silver oak (grevillea robusta). this study was carried out within 12 private coffee estates canopy_dominant

[00_readme.txt]
this dataset contains data on bird communities from variable-width line transect surveys carried out in 1995-96 in the mudumalai wildlife sanctuary (now tiger reserve) and upper nilgiris, tamil nadu, india. the data were collected on a project of the centre for ecological sciences, indian institute of science, bangalore.

geographical area: mudumalai wildlife sanctuary (now tiger reserve) and upper nilgiris, tamil nadu, india

taxonomic scope: birds

acknowledgement: i am grateful to dr r. sukumar for the opportunity to survey these transects and to p. pavithra and palani for help with data.

methods

bird data are from 1200 m long (0.75 miles) line transect surveys surveyed typically in about 100-120 min duration in the early morning hours. the methods for bird sampling are as described in raman (2003) and in this doctoral thesis:
raman, t. r. s. 2001. community ecology and conservation of mid-elevation tropical rainforest bird communities in the southern western ghats, india. phd thesis, indian institute of science, bangalore.

all transects were censused during the first 3 h after sunrise when bird activity was highest in the area walking at a slow, uniform pace. all birds seen (perched or flying under the canopy) or heard were recorded as to species, number (wherever possible) and perpendicular distance in the following metre classes: 0–5, 5–10, etcwith the further distance classes being wider to minimize errors in distance estimation.
